SMTO-SYS-0004 — SMTO's own network connections failed, so the task stopped

GUID: 13356566-167a-449c-ab89-8832a455879d
Slug: transport-runtime-failure
Domain: SYS · Subsystem: runtime

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use network connections on the computer it runs on, often because that computer ran low on memory or on connections it can open at once. SMTO stopped the task; work already saved is still there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close programs you don't need on the computer running SMTO, or ask the person who manages it to check that it has enough free memory. This failure usually means that computer ran out of memory or of connections it can open at once.
  2. Open the task's activity and check what the task already did before continuing. A request SMTO was sending when it failed may or may not have arrived, so SMTO won't resend it on its own.
  3. Type /restart to restart SMTO, then open the task and select Resume, or Restart task if Resume isn't shown. The restart also interrupts other running tasks. The task stays blocked until SMTO restarts, and a restart releases the connections it was holding.

What success looks like

  • After the restart, the task continues and no new connection error appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they include the system error code. Don't repeat an action until you've confirmed whether it already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A source-owned socket or selector operation failed locally (EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOMEM, ENOBUFS, EBADF or a failed resolver thread), or a saved connection-retry reservation was interrupted, so the run is blocked as a transport runtime fault.

What this means

  • A source-owned socket or selector operation failed, exhausted process resources, or lost an in-flight retry reservation. Automatic model recovery cannot repair this failure.

Why this can happen

  • A source-owned socket or selector operation failed, exhausted process resources, or lost an in-flight retry reservation. Automatic model recovery cannot repair this failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the source phase and OS error code. Compare active registrations, created and released counts, owner age and process descriptors to distinguish exhaustion from an invalid selector operation.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Inspect the transport facts in the run's runtime.fault_blocked event (phase, os_error, code, aggregate handle counts). For transport_resource_exhausted raise the open-file limit (ulimit -n) or free memory and handles; for transport_invariant or transport_retry_interrupted look for handle leaks. Restart the Server to clear the per-generation blocker, and never replay a request whose transmission is uncertain.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the retained phase, OS error code and aggregate handle counts. Correct the runtime failure before continuing.

How to verify the fix

  • Matching evidence confirms the connection or process state.

What not to do

  • Do not replay an operation whose transmission or outcome is uncertain.

Technical notes

  • Do not replay an operation whose transmission or outcome is uncertain.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
